target_customer: Privacy conscious individuals first, then enterprises and governments that need to detect spyware and unwanted data transmission on mobile devices
problem: Zero click spyware and apps can record or transmit data from a phone without the user knowing, and signature based scanners miss new spyware.
business_model: Consumer mobile security app (freemium) with planned enterprise and government offerings

founders.name: Maria Terzi
education: PhD, machine learning and recommender systems
founders.background_notes: YC bio: won two Google hackathons during her PhD and has R&D experience in machine learning and private AI; the page lists Google under employers but the bio reads as hackathon and research experience, so it is not recorded as employment. KIOS (University of Cyprus research centre) says the founders are KIOS alumni.

founders.name: Liza Charalambous
education: PhD, machine learning (signal processing, AI, digital communications)
founders.background_notes: YC bio: digital security expert with over 8 years of cyber security project experience.

founders.name: Artemis Kontou
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch (September 2021); not on the fetched YC page.

competitors.name: Apple and Google built in camera and microphone indicators
competitors.what: OS level indicators that spyware can bypass according to TechCrunch

competitors.name: Malwarebytes
competitors.what: Mobile security app with stalkerware detection

technical_complexity.rationale: On device machine learning that detects abnormal activity and zero click spyware behavior without signatures is hard for a two PhD team; the founders trained models themselves.

defensibility.rationale: Behavioral detection models and on device data could compound, but OS vendors and large antivirus firms can add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple and Google already shipped basic indicators; no incumbent acquisition of Malloc was found through 2026.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported over 80,000 monthly active users for the Antistalker app within months of its 2021 launch, and stalkerware and spyware risk was widely discussed.

branding.domain_note: Company site is mallocprivacy.com, not malloc.com (malloc is a standard C memory allocation function).
branding.brand_signature: Antistalker, the first consumer app brand
branding.community_and_virality: Antistalker was launched on Product Hunt (listing seen in search).

brand_strength.rationale: The name is a programming term that is hard to search for (search results are dominated by the C function) but the Antistalker product name is clear; limited brand coverage beyond TechCrunch.

pivots.why: Cyprus Mail headline describes taking Malloc from a privacy app to Europe's defence frontline; article not opened

outcome_analysis: Malloc, a Cyprus based mobile spyware detection company, launched the Antistalker app and reached over 80,000 monthly users in 2021, then raised nearly 2 million dollars from YC and the Urban Innovation Fund. It later won research grants and appears to be shifting toward defence customers. No Series A, acquisition or shutdown was found, so it is a small active company still in an early stage.
notes: Seed of almost 2M is stated by TechCrunch and KIOS (University of Cyprus); Seedtable lists about 130K in Aug 2021 (aggregator, not recorded). A pre-seed grant from Cyprus RIF exists but its amount was not found. Founding year is 2021 per YC and 2020 per KIOS. The pivot entry rests on a headline only; treat as unverified. Company site was not fetched directly.
